title: Provision resources securely: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: What must be approved, baselined, registered, and accepted before this resource enters service?
focalInsight: Provisioning joins accountable purpose, safe defaults, baseline, inventory, authorization, and lifecycle planning.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Secure Provisioning
nodes.definition: Controlled transition of a resource into service with owned purpose and approved safeguards.
nodes.detail: Controlled transition of a resource into service with owned purpose and approved safeguards.
nodes.decision: Require request, owner, purpose, classification, environment, dependencies, approval, acceptance evidence.
nodes.failureExample: A production SaaS tenant appears without inventory or owner.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Provisioning is controlled entry, not mere creation.

nodes.label: Secure Defaults
nodes.definition: Initial settings that reduce exposure before local customization.
nodes.detail: Initial settings that reduce exposure before local customization.
nodes.decision: Use hardened approved images, least privilege, secure protocols, secrets handling, and disabled unnecessary features.
nodes.failureExample: A new database is internet reachable with default credentials.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Defaults must be safe before exceptions.

nodes.label: Baseline
nodes.definition: Approved reference configuration used for build, assessment, and drift detection.
nodes.detail: Approved reference configuration used for build, assessment, and drift detection.
nodes.decision: Define version, parameters, owner, exception, measurement, and change path.
nodes.failureExample: A host passes build but no reference exists to detect later change.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Baseline makes compliance and drift observable.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.definition: Approved decision to activate resource, access, or change within defined scope.
nodes.detail: Approved decision to activate resource, access, or change within defined scope.
nodes.decision: Confirm authority, business purpose, risk, dependencies, and evidence before activation.
nodes.failureExample: Engineer enables production access because deployment succeeded.

nodes.label: Configuration Drift
nodes.definition: Difference between actual configuration and approved baseline.
nodes.detail: Difference between actual configuration and approved baseline.
nodes.decision: Monitor change, owner, exception, and remediation trigger.
nodes.failureExample: A firewall rule remains after emergency work and creates exposure.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Drift requires reconciliation or risk decision.

nodes.label: Asset Inventory
nodes.definition: Lifecycle record linking resource to owner, location, purpose, configuration, support, and retirement.
nodes.detail: Lifecycle record linking resource to owner, location, purpose, configuration, support, and retirement.
nodes.decision: Register before production and reconcile with discovery.
nodes.failureExample: Unmanaged VM is not assessed or patched.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Inventory is a provisioning gate and lifecycle control.

nodes.label: Data Lifecycle
nodes.definition: Managed states from collection through use, storage, archive, and destruction.
nodes.detail: Managed states from collection through use, storage, archive, and destruction.
nodes.decision: Plan data purpose, copies, retention, protections, and end state before activation.
nodes.failureExample: New service creates backups with no retention/disposal plan.
